title: A Pilgrim and a Stranger
description: A Pilgrim and a Stranger in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Paul Gerhardt, first published in 1666. The English translation is by Jane Laurie Borthwick (1858). The tune, PASSION CHORALE, is by Hans Leo Hassler (1601). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: A Pil-grim and a stran-ger, I jour-ney here_ be-low; Far dis-tant is my coun-try The home to which_ I go. Here I_ must toil and tra-vel, Oft wea-ry and op-prest, But there_ my God shall lead me To e-ver-las-ting rest.

lines: The home to which I go.
Here I must toil and travel,
But there my God shall lead me
I've met with storm and danger,
There's nothing here that tempts me
It is a well worn pathway,
And them I fain would follow,
Like them in life and death!
Thank God, the end will come!
The land of light and love.
